# Functions Capability Workflow

## 1. Inspect before asking

Locate the requested `*.Functions` host, its `Program.cs`, package references, `AGENTS.md`, `host.json` and corresponding `*.Test.Functions` project. Read the Functions instructions and relevant sections of the installed package guide. Use the existing host if unambiguous; ask which deployment only when several candidates fit.

Resolve shared-core versus standalone from actual business-project references, not naming or package management. CPM is independent: standalone hosts can use central versions. Read existing root/host guidance and cross-check actual provider artefacts; stop on disagreement. Do not demand missing root Feature Configuration or generate business layers to change a standalone function. Route an explicitly requested missing baseline/Test.Common retrofit through `coreex-scaffold`.

If the host is missing, route explicit host-creation work through `coreex-scaffold`. A request to change a function does not authorize creating another deployment. Never re-run a template with `--force` over a customized host.

Inspect existing dependencies and nearby patterns first. The Functions package currently brings HTTP/Service Bus dependencies transitively; only add explicit packages when required by the project's direct-dependency policy or a missing binding. Follow effective CPM in both shared/standalone modes, with inline versions only when disabled. Preserve explicit opt-outs and existing compatible pins. Reuse the actual Test.Common reference for shared fixtures/resources; it is test-only and not a database/broker scaffold.

## 2. Resolve the actual behavior

Ask one short question at a time, only for decisions not established by the request or code. Do not mechanically ask every question below.

| Trigger | Unresolved decisions that affect implementation |
|---|---|
| HTTP | Verb/route, input/output shape, function authorization and application identity/tenant policy, idempotency need, existing application operation versus new processing. Function keys are not user identity. |
| Service Bus | Queue or topic/subscription, setting names, session/batch needs, uniform native JSON versus CloudEvents dispatch, invalid-data/business/transient dispositions, duplicate handling. |
| Blob | Container/path/connection, Event Grid versus polling source, payload limits/format, current blob versus exact historical revision, output/side effects, content rejection versus operational retry. |
| Timer | Schedule/timezone/deployment settings, missed runs, replay/overlap tolerance, retry policy and cancellation behavior. |

Explicit settlement examples cover non-session single-message Service Bus delivery. Do not silently extend the bridge to batches or assume session behavior is proven; verify the exact binding/API and add runtime evidence for those requirements. Other triggers remain native and need their own verified semantics, not an invented CoreEx abstraction.

For any side effect, establish at-least-once/duplicate behavior. Blob-to-broker forwarding is not transactional; sending then failing can duplicate messages. Output bindings are not outboxes. Add stable identities, transactional invariants or duplicate-tolerant processing as requirements dictate; do not promise exactly-once.

Present a compact implementation plan covering host/capability, processing location, required dependencies/settings, failure policy and tests. Existing authorization to implement remains valid; ask again only if unresolved behavior materially changes scope.

## 3. Compose only what this capability needs

Create capability folders on demand, for example `Imports/ImportFunction.cs` plus `Imports/BlobForwarder.cs`. Put transport-local DTOs, binding constants and mappings beside their functions; do not force one folder per attributed method or create a speculative `Shared` folder. Keep function names unique within the app.

For shared-core, reuse application contracts/services and invoke the existing L1 skills only for their actual scope: contract, validator, service, repository, policy or adapter. Configure database/cache/outbox/adapters before registering services that depend on them. The empty template deliberately does not scan all assemblies; `AddDynamicServicesUsing` is appropriate when every discovered service's dependencies are wired. Register a focused service explicitly if a broad scan would pull in unrelated dependencies.

For standalone, delegate to focused local handlers and register them in DI. Capability-local types do not require new projects. Extract shared libraries only for demonstrated complexity/reuse; use CoreEx validators/results/events when useful, not by ritual.

Use the [verified patterns](patterns.md) and trigger-specific rules below.

### HTTP

Call `ConfigureFunctionsWebApplication()` immediately after builder creation, before `UseCoreExExecutionContext()`. Register MVC services and MVC `WebApi`; opt into `ConvertUnhandledExceptionsToProblemDetails` when that helper is the intended unexpected-error boundary. It does not catch failures outside WebApi. Reuse its JSON/validation/status/Location behavior and pass the invocation cancellation token.

For POST idempotency, use `FunctionWithIdempotencyAsync` explicitly and return its result directly; `[IdempotencyKey]` alone does not activate this path. Add the configured provider and cache only when requested. Defer application execution inside the callback, use the same configured WebApi instance, and do not use eager rendering for streaming or extra HTTP output bindings. Explain best-effort retention/body limits and lack of default cross-instance mutual exclusion; Redis L2 alone is not a distributed lock.

Do not install ASP.NET routing, `MapControllers`, NSwag middleware, `UseCoreExExceptionHandler`, `UseIdempotencyKey` or `MapHealthChecks` on the worker builder. Health is an optional HTTP capability for an operational requirement, never an automatic scaffold addition.

### Service Bus

Choose native binding processing for simple workloads; add the CoreEx bridge when classified subscriber handling/settlement is useful. CloudEvents use `ServiceBusSubscribedSubscriber` with `SubscribedManager`/event formatter and application subscribers. Uniform JSON can use `ServiceBusSubscriberBase<T>` with its validator and explicit error policy, without CloudEvents/subject dispatch. A callback bridge owns its own parsing, classification and logging.

For either bridge overload, disable auto-completion, pass the same queue or topic/subscription expression used by the trigger and thread cancellation. `%SettingName%` paths resolve via ambient worker configuration for metric labels; listener settings must also exist in the Functions host. Choose malformed/validation/business policies explicitly: CoreEx defaults can complete invalid work as error rather than dead-lettering it.

Success completes, classified retry abandons once, dead-letter settles once; unclassified/catastrophic failure or invocation cancellation propagates without bridge settlement. Never settle a second time after failure. The bridge adds no receiver retry loop, pause/resume or receiver-level circuit breaker; prefer a Subscribe host when those controls are required.

### Blob

Use native `BlobTrigger`/SDK binding and only the required storage extension/client registrations. With Event Grid source, plan subscription provisioning separately; local Azurite notification tests do not prove Azure Event Grid delivery/authentication.

For schema-defined CSV, use `coreex-file` to generate the wire model, mapping, validator, context, processor and create-only handler from `*-file.yaml`; keep the Functions trigger thin and use the Azure Storage SDK for input/report operations. A durable per-unit receipt, business mutation and outbox write belong in one supported application transaction; report persistence is separate and cannot make trigger delivery exactly-once.

Bound payload processing. Separate logged content rejection from operational failure; do not swallow read/write failures as success. A `BlobClient` targets the current blob, not an immutable event revision. Use ETag-conditional reads or versions/snapshots as needed and deterministic output identity for replay. Provision output containers outside handler execution. Storage extension retries/poison queues are not Service Bus settlement policies.

### Timer

Use native `TimerTrigger("%ScheduleSetting%")`; configure the schedule in Functions host settings, not solely worker `appsettings.json`. Delegate the workload and pass cancellation. Do not add a competing hosted-service scheduler, enable run-on-startup automatically or describe invocation failure as guaranteed redelivery. Confirm timer retry/monitoring/timezone support against the selected plan/runtime before configuring it.

## 4. Configure and record

Add required imports to `GlobalUsing.cs`, sorted ordinally. Add only needed packages and host/worker settings. `host.json` settings affect the whole Function App: check impact on sibling functions before changing concurrency, retries or routing. Deployment identity/network/configuration is app-wide even where scale groups differ.

Binding connection/schedule/entity settings must reach the Functions host through app settings or local settings. Worker-only configuration is insufficient. Never commit secrets; keep a credential-free example or documented setting names because `local.settings.json` is ignored and not published. Do not generate infrastructure inside handlers.

Update the host's `AGENTS.md` with capability names, shared/local processing, binding setting names, authorization/failure policy and test/runtime requirements. Preserve root Feature Configuration; update it only when the change really enables a shared solution feature. Do not add health/telemetry infrastructure by default.

## 5. Add and execute meaningful tests

Mirror capability folders in the generated host test project. Use `FunctionTester.Create<TFunction>()` against the real host entry point so startup/DI and worker middleware execute. Use NUnit/AwesomeAssertions and existing CoreEx test helpers; no fabricated empty-success fixture.

For HTTP, assert exact status/body/important headers and representative validation/error/cancellation behavior. `ToHttpResponseMessageAssertor(request)` renders deferred results; use `SnapshotHttpResponse(request.HttpContext.Response)` with a readable/seekable buffer for idempotency's already-written response. Prove replay skips the operation if adding idempotency.

For Service Bus, assert exact settlement count/action, no settlement on propagated failure/cancellation, failure during settlement with no second attempt, and `AutoCompleteMessages = false`. Validate the chosen poison policy with actual malformed/invalid payloads. For Blob/Timer, prove original input/token delegation, effect/rejection behavior and bubbling operational failure; add replay/revision tests where required.

Pure boundary tests can replace a local handler to observe delegation; tests claiming persisted business behavior must use the owned database/cache/outbox, with inter-domain dependencies mocked per existing policy. Keep test layers distinct instead of duplicating every service rule.

Build the affected test project then run the narrowest relevant tests. For required runtime claims, extend the existing Core Tools/Aspire topology instead of creating a second Contoso sample: real HTTP binding, broker settlement/redelivery, Blob notification/poison behavior. Use existing infrastructure ownership and cleanup; missing infrastructure is an explicit verification gap, not grounds for weaker assertions.

Invocation tests do not prove trigger delivery, binding conversion, authorization enforcement or cloud provisioning. Report those limits honestly; never claim an invocation test proves function-key enforcement.
